plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like blooms. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with single, semi-double, and fully double flower forms. It thrives in partial shade and acidic soils, and is a staple of winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak January to March)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that produces all true tea, and camellia seed oil has been used in Japan for centuries as a hair and skin treatment.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped flowers borne on tall, sturdy stalks. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, garden-grown and wild relatives bloom outdoors, while in the north, potted bulbs flower indoors in winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Native to Central and South America and the Caribbean; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Hippeastrum bulbs can bloom within 6 to 8 weeks of planting, and a single large bulb can send up multiple flower stalks in one season.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous shrub that blooms on bare branches in the dead of winter. Its spidery, ribbon-like petals are strongly fragrant and curl up in freezing weather to protect themselves, unfurling again when it warms.
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel petals can curl tightly in cold weather and re-expand when temperatures rise, allowing the flowers to survive repeated freezes.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like foliage and a broad umbrella canopy. Under the Southern Hemisphere's summer sun, it becomes covered with brilliant clusters of large flowers, each with one distinctive spotted petal.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in tropical regions during the dry season
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including northern Australia, Brazil, and Africa
plants.funFact: Despite being one of the most celebrated tropical flowering trees, the royal poinciana is endangered in its native Madagascar.
